items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Keg Johnson used to call me -- Budd's brother -- all the time and say, Trummy, that's fantastic. How can you play that high. You know, he used to call me.

ctx.x: Yeah, but they really didn't -- with Earl's band you had a chance to show yourself, you know, to play. He would let you play. You know, on a broadcast we used to broadcast every night out of the Grand Terrace. And the guys with Cab used to call me all the way from Texas. Say man, that sure is a good trombone player -- solo you played, Trummy. Keg Johnson used to call me -- Budd's brother -- all the time and say, Trummy, that's fantastic. How can you play that high. You know, he used to call me. And these -- this…

It was real encouragement, you know, for you to do things. And that's why they tried to get me with Cab's band back there then, but I wouldn't go, you know. I told them I wouldn't go. I said if I got with your band, you think I'd get those kind of solos to play. And Cab said, yeah, that makes sense. You'd make money but you wouldn't be -- I didn't need money then. I was foot loose and free, you know, so I didn't need no lot of money and I just enjoyed playing. I really almost didn't go with Lunceford from Earl…
